subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for requester agents, and what public config/API shape should own that security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix adds public config surface and changes security-sensitive inheritance semantics between requester agents and spawned children.

options.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
options.body: Add a documented selfDeny/delegateOnly-style field with deny precedence, /tools visibility, inherited policy tests, and ACP/runtime behavior explicitly defined.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy design
options.body: Keep this issue open until the per-spawn tool restriction design also covers requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.

options.title: Reject new core surface
options.body: Document separate agent IDs or behavior-level delegation as the supported pattern, accepting that config-enforced separation of duties remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add a documented selfDeny/delegateOnly-style field with deny precedence, /tools visibility, inherited policy tests, and ACP/runtime behavior explicitly defined.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined signal from recent tool-policy/docs history and prior review routing for this security/config decision.
